text_blocks.snippet: Mental illness is a prevalent health issue in the United States, affecting millions of adults. Nearly 1 in 5 adults experience a mental illness in a given year, with a significant percentage also experiencing a serious mental illness. These illnesses encompass a range of conditions, from mild to severe, and can significantly impact a person's thoughts, mood, and behavior.
snippet_highlighted_words: Nearly 1 in 5 adults experience a mental illness in a given year, with a significant percentage also experiencing a serious mental illness

text_blocks.snippet: Here's a more detailed look at the prevalence of mental illness in the US:

list.title: Any Mental Illness (AMI):
list.snippet: In 2022, over 59.3 million adults (23.1%) in the US experienced a mental illness.

list.title: Serious Mental Illness (SMI):
list.snippet: A subset of AMI, SMI affects a smaller, more severe portion of the population. About 5.86% of adults experience SMI.

list.title: Age:
list.snippet: Mental illness rates vary by age group. In 2023, young adults aged 18-25 had the highest rate of mental illness at 33.8%, according to USAFacts.

list.title: Substance Use Disorders:
list.snippet: A significant number of individuals also experience substance use disorders alongside mental health conditions.

list.title: Demographics:
list.snippet: Factors like race, ethnicity, and socioeconomic status can influence mental health outcomes.

list.title: Social and Economic Conditions:
list.snippet: The social and economic environment in which people live can also play a role in their mental well-being.

list.title: COVID-19 Pandemic:
list.snippet: The pandemic has highlighted the impact of stress, isolation, and economic hardship on mental health, according to PlanStreet.
Suicide: Suicide is a leading cause of death, especially among young adults.
Co-occurring Disorders: Mental health conditions and substance use disorders often occur together, creating a complex set of challenges.

list.title: Importance of Early Intervention:
list.snippet: Addressing mental health issues early on is crucial for improving outcomes, especially during childhood and adolescence, according to the CDC.

list.title: Treatment Options:
list.snippet: Treatment for mental illness can include psychotherapy, medication, or a combination of both.

list.title: Seeking Help:
list.snippet: Individuals can seek help from their primary care provider, mental health professionals, or through various federal resources from the National Institute of Mental Health (NIMH).
